title: Redwood data retention demo - SilverStream Payments
summary: Live demo of Redwood Console / API controls for data handling and retention. Covered request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII masking, per-route retention settings, KMS integration, and audit logs. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated for payments workloads; security and data residency are primary concerns. Agreed next steps: send SOC2 docs, share retention config examples, schedule pilot for end of July.
topics: Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs for payments workloads
Demo of Console UI and API toggles
Optimize recommendations for cost vs retention
transcript:
[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya Chen from Redwood, AE on the account. Ravi, Jordan — you on?
[00:06] Ravi: Yep, here, Ravi Patel, solutions engineer. Hi Carlos, Anika, Tom.
[00:12] Carlos: Hi all. Good to meet you. We got 45 minutes, right?
[00:18] Maya: Yep, 45, trying to run through the controls and leave time for Q&A. Quick agenda — show Console UI for data retention, the API flags for request storage, how PII redaction works, and the audit/KMS pieces.
[00:30] Anika: Great, security lead on our side. Main ask: we cannot persist cardholder data in any logs, and we need proof for audits (SOC2). Also want options to keep minimal metadata for troubleshooting.
[00:42] Tom: And we need to know performance impact — latency vs turning off certain caches.
[00:48] Ravi: Totally. We'll call out dedicated vs hosted tradeoffs as well. First, quick show of Console. (screen share)
[01:05] Ravi: On the Console, we have per-route retention. You can set store/no-store at the route level, or per-model. Here on this route we toggle "Request Storage" to off — that means payloads don't persist to object store or long-term logs. Only ephemeral tracing is kept for the duration of the request for debugging, depending on your setting.
[01:35] Carlos: Is ephemeral tracing masked? Payment numbers?
[01:39] Ravi: By default we run automated redaction on PII patterns — card numbers, SSNs, emails — but you can also configure custom regex redaction rules or a transformation pipeline. There's an option called "PII Masking Level" with presets: minimal, strict, custom.
[02:00] Maya: To add, for customers in regulated sectors we recommend Strict + KMS-backed pseudonymization, which replaces tokens client-side or server-side depending on policy.
[02:12] Anika: Client-side? We need to avoid sending PAN at all to third-party servers.
[02:17] Jordan: Good callout — we support client-side tokenization integrations and also request-level no-store so PAN never lands in persistent logs. But if you need model input for inference you either tokenize before send or use a dedicated private deployment where the whole stack is inside your VPC.
[02:35] Tom: Performance hit on dedicated vs hosted?
[02:38] Ravi: Dedicated gives you predictable throughput and you can pin models; network latency will vary based on your VPC configuration but we avoid cross-tenant logging. Hosted with store=no-store also works but you must evaluate your compliance posture.
[02:54] Maya: Now API demo — toggle via a header or SDK flag. Here's an example curl:
[03:00] Maya: curl -H "x-redwood-store: no" ...
[03:06] Maya: That header disables request storage for that call. We also have per-tenant defaults and route overrides.
[03:12] Carlos: If someone accidentally sends PAN without header, can we retroactively delete?
[03:18] Ravi: We have an expunge API for stored requests and a log purge workflow; retention policies can be set to auto-delete after X days. We also keep separate audit logs (who toggled what) — those are minimal, but we can redact the payload content in audit entries.
[03:36] Anika: How are audit logs protected? HSM?
[03:39] Jordan: Audit logs are encrypted at rest. For keys you can use Redwood-managed KMS or integrate your own KMS/HSM. We can also set up dedicated HSM in private deployments for customers that require FIPS/HSM-backed keys.
[03:54] Tom: Sounds good. What about downstream debug artifacts — transcripts we send to SRE?
[03:59] Ravi: Those are governed by retention rules; you can enable only anonymized traces or set to keep only metadata like duration, latency, error codes. We also have an "anonymize user content" toggle that replaces values with stable pseudonyms so you can correlate sessions without exposing raw PII.
[04:18] Carlos: Do you have examples of redaction failing or false positives?
[04:22] Ravi: We do; redaction uses pattern matching plus ML-based entity detection. There's a quality tradeoff; we provide a preview tool in the Console so you can test sample payloads and view what would be redacted. We recommend running your production prompts through the preview before enabling automatic purge.
[04:40] Anika: We'll want to run that. Also need SOC2 report and encryption attestations.
[04:45] Maya: We'll send the security pack after this meeting — SOC2, pen test summary, data flow diagram.
[04:52] Tom: Great.
[05:00] Maya: Next, demo of the Optimize recommendations — how to tradeoff cost vs retention. (switch) Here Optimize flags routes that cost more because of heavy context retention and suggests quantization or shorter context windows. For retention, you can set a short-term buffer for debugging — like 24 hours — then auto-delete.
[05:30] Carlos: If we set 24 hours, can we export those logs to our S3 before deletion?
[05:35] Ravi: Yes, we support export hooks to customer buckets (configured in the Console). Exports are encrypted with your KMS if you opt in.
[05:45] Anika: How about SSO — we need SAML and RBAC for internal roles.
[05:50] Jordan: We support SAML/SSO, SCIM for provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. Actions like changing retention settings require elevated roles and are logged.
[06:03] Tom: Competitors? Are you referencing anything obvious in market?
[06:06] Maya: Customers often compare us to OpenAI for simplicity and to Anthropic/AWS Bedrock for enterprise features. We focus on control and observability.
[06:15] Carlos: Any showstoppers? We need KYC data redaction and region-specific residency.
[06:20] Ravi: For residency we can pin deployments to region or run Private (VPC/on-prem) where data never leaves your network. For KYC, you can configure custom redaction pipelines and we can run a one-off PII scrub during onboarding.
[06:38] Anika: Let's talk about logs retention policies. We need a default 30-day retention for telemetry, but PII zero retention.
[06:45] Maya: That's doable — set default telemetry 30d, and route-level PII rules to no-store. We can also create an automated rule: any payload flagged as PAN or SSN is auto-expunge.
[06:58] Carlos: How do you surface when the auto-expunge ran? We need audit trails.
[07:03] Jordan: Expunge events are stored in the audit log and include timestamp, actor, request id. The payload is not included.
[07:12] Tom: Can you show the API call to purge?
[07:15] Ravi: Sure. POST /v1/admin/expunge with filter { request_id, created_before } — we'll send exact examples in the follow-up.
[07:28] Anika: Do you retain embeddings or cached values? Embeddings could leak content.
[07:33] Ravi: Good point. You can disable embedding storage and caching per-route. We also provide deterministic hashing for embedding keys if you need to track without storing vectors.
[07:47] Carlos: Any impact to latency when you disable KV cache?
[07:50] Ravi: Disabling KV cache increases token-generation latency for multi-turn sessions; Optimize suggests batching or a smaller context window to compensate. We'll share benchmark numbers from similar customers.
[08:02] Maya: Quick Q&A — Carlos: what would a pilot look like?
[08:06] Carlos: We want to test 2 everyday flows: refund processing logic and KYC extraction, with store=no-store for refunds, and pseudonymized KYC for analytics.
[08:15] Maya: Sounds good — propose a 4-week pilot on Dedicated dev pool or hosted with private tenancy. We'll provide a test plan and cost estimate.
[08:25] Tom: Timeline — we aim to decide by mid-August.
[08:29] Maya: Next steps: security pack, retention config examples, pilot proposal, and scheduling a benchmark.
[08:36] Anika: Also send the preview tool and sample regex rules.
[08:40] Ravi: Will do.
[08:44] (ambient chatter, misc clarifications)
[09:12] Maya: I think we're close on time, last question?
[09:16] Carlos: No, that's it. Thanks.
[09:20] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with notes.
[09:25] (call ends)
